editorial: Despite being a relatively small tropical island, Sri Lanka has distinct micro-climates along its northeast and southwest coasts.
We’d argue that the route we took along the southwest coast and into the central highlands are more worth your while. So we suggest going during the dry season (December to April) in these parts.
Our own trip was in March, when the temperatures were beginning to creep into the mid-30s °C (low-90s °F) in Sigiriya and Ella. If that is not your cup of Ceylon tea, go earlier in the season.
The wet season (May to September) in these parts are the best time to visit the northeast if you fancy surfing in Arugam Bay or elephant watching in Minneriya National Park.
The rest of the year has unpredictable weather, including the risk of cyclones, across the island.

seasons.title: October & November
editorial: This is a weird time of the year with the south-west monsoon receding and the north-east monsoon gathering momentum. The weather is unpredictable across the island with the possibility of cyclones further dampening the odds of a great trip.
